request: Analyze GSE267512 for PMID 39393048 (Bioavailable testosterone and androgen receptor activation, but not total testosterone, are associated with muscle mass and strength in females.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq, vastus lateralis biopsies, human pre-menopausal untrained females
final.primary_estimand: Within-person change in the muscle transcriptome from before (PRE) to after (POST) a 12-week supervised resistance-training programme (the transcriptomic arm of a testosterone-association paper).
planned_contrasts: POST vs PRE resistance training (S3.6.p1: 214 DEGs, 122 up, 92 down)
final.paper_method: DESeq2, model Genes ~ ID + timepoint (ID accounts for repeated measures) (S2.14.p6)
final.paper_filter: genes with mean across all samples <= 10 reads removed, 14,979 genes retained (S2.12.6.p1)
final.paper_samples: 35 pre-training, 27 post-training biopsies (FIG7 legend; S3.p1: 35 enrolled, 27 completed)
final.paper_results: 214 DEGs POST vs PRE, 122 up, 92 down, FDR<0.05; ChEA3 TF enrichment on DEGs (AR ranked 284/1632)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.14.p6 gives DESeq2 ~ID+timepoint, S2.14.p7 FDR<0.05 with no fold-change rule, S3.6.p1/FIG7 report 214 DEGs (122 up/92 down). The training is resistance exercise, so this is an exercise-effect transcriptomic contrast (repeated measures, pre/post).

checks: GEO treatment_protocol: 27 pre-menopausal untrained females, 12-week resistance training, PRE/POST biopsies
vastus lateralis, human, Kallisto, TruSeq Ribo-Zero as in paper methods

ownership.reasoning: Paper data availability names GSE267512; GEO description matches the cohort, biopsy site, and sequencing protocol.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix column names equal GEO title exactly (57/57). Title = 4-letter participant code + PRE/POST. subject (33 participants, 24 with both samples, 9 with a single biopsy) and time derived from the title by regex; exact key match, no positional alignment.

matrix.reasoning: GeneCounts_RAW_DATA wide file: non-negative integers, library sizes 20-29M, GEO data_processing says aligned raw gene counts from Kallisto transcript counts (estimated counts summarized to genes, stored as integers), paper uses DESeq2. Treated as rounded estimated counts. The 3col.tsv long-format file is the same data and is not used. The matrix was pre-filtered with the paper's rule (mean count across samples > 10) by prep_filter.py: 14,828 genes retained vs the paper's 14,979 (the paper's sample set is larger).

design.subject: subject
design.reasoning: Paper contrast is POST vs PRE with participant ID as a blocking term. Only one treatment column (characteristics_ch1.4.treatment = PRE/POST, identical to the title suffix) exists; no alternative contrast. All 57 deposited samples are kept (the paper model also keeps unpaired samples via the ID term); 9 participants with only one biopsy contribute to the ID parameter only. The GEO series has 31 PRE/26 POST, versus 35/27 in the paper: 4 PRE and 1 POST sample are not deposited.

covariance.reasoning: Repeated biopsies from the same participant: subject is a blocking term as in the paper (~ID+timepoint). No other covariates in the paper model; age is a donor attribute not used by the paper.

paper_route.reason: same model and contrast executed with pydeseq2 instead of R DESeq2

deviations: gene filter applied by mean count > 10 (paper text says mean RPM <= 10 removed, but its 14,979 retained genes match a count-scale filter)
sample set 57 vs the paper 62 biopsies

method.reasoning: Paper-stated DESeq2 with subject blocking is directly executable on integer counts. A complete-pairs-only run is added as a sensitivity analysis.

threshold.reasoning: S2.14.p7: significant at FDR-adjusted P < 0.05; no fold-change cutoff stated. Audit rule with |log2FC| > log2(1.5) is only for comparison.

caveats: 57 of the paper 62 biopsies are deposited
paper reports no gene list in the main text

study.reasoning: Same model, contrast, filter and threshold as the paper; counts compared to 214 (122 up / 92 down).

discrepancies.data: 31 PRE and 26 POST deposited (24 complete pairs, 9 single)
mean count > 10 gives 14,828 genes (mean RPM>10 would leave only 6,084)
ChEA3 not available in the executors; paper reports no GO/KEGG/GSEA

executions.name: time_POST_vs_PRE
executions.reasoning: paper model ~ID+timepoint on all deposited samples

executions.name: time_POST_vs_PRE_pairs_only
executions.reasoning: restrict to the 24 participants with both biopsies
